author: The Infographics Show
description:
Gen Z hasn’t simply decided it doesn’t want kids. In fact, most young people still say they want families. The problem is that many no longer believe they can afford the future that raising children requires.

This video explores why Gen Z is delaying or abandoning parenthood as housing costs explode, gig work replaces stable careers, childcare and healthcare become increasingly expensive, and AI threatens the entry-level jobs young workers depend on to build financial security. We also examine why falling birth rates persist even in countries with generous parental leave and government subsidies. From South Korea to Scandinavia, cash incentives have struggled to reverse a deeper problem. Young adults increasingly lack confidence that their lives will become more stable with time.
Meanwhile, older generations continue to hold a disproportionate share of wealth, property, and government support, leaving younger people to fund systems they’re not convinced will exist for them later.

title: Why Gen Z DON'T WANT Kids

description:
Keeping money in a savings account feels responsible. But if your interest rate is lower than inflation, your balance can go up while your actual wealth quietly disappears.

This video explores why traditional saving can become a financial trap. During periods of high inflation and low interest rates, cash loses purchasing power year after year, even when the number in your account barely changes. It’s the “money illusion” that makes people feel safe while their savings buy less and less. We also examine how Federal Reserve policy, quantitative easing, falling savings yields, and sudden economic shocks can work against ordinary savers. And even money left untouched isn’t always safe, dormant accounts can eventually be transferred to state unclaimed-property systems if owners stop actively managing them.

title: If YOU Are 'Saving' Money, You NEED To Stop!

description:
We’ve mapped planets, tracked thousands of asteroids, and sent probes beyond Pluto. But directly above and below the Sun lies a region of space we barely monitor, and it may be one of the most important blind spots in our entire planetary defense system.

This video explores what exists beyond the flat orbital plane of our solar system, why reaching the Sun’s polar regions is so difficult, and how the laws of orbital mechanics effectively trap most spacecraft inside the ecliptic. NASA’s Ulysses mission managed to escape that plane once, and discovered chaotic magnetic fields, extreme solar winds, and an environment far more violent than scientists expected.
The problem goes beyond understanding the Sun. Interstellar objects like ‘Oumuamua can approach from steep angles that are much harder for our observatories to detect, potentially giving humanity far less warning if something dangerous ever heads directly toward Earth.
